newsitem.title: USA: U.S. approves airline liability agreements.
newsitem.headline: U.S. approves airline liability agreements.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday approved three inter-airline accords boosting compensation for injury and death of international passengers by lifting limits on the amounts that can be claimed.

The decision, announced by the Transportation Department, also relieves passengers and their families from the need to prove an airline was at fault in order to receive full compensation for death and injury.

Under the previous standard, set out in the post-World War Two Warsaw Convention, liability was limited to $75,000 in the United States unless the airline could be proved guilty of "willful misconduct." Other limits ranged from $150,000 in most of Europe to $350,000 in Australia.

"With today's action, we are taking an historic step towards realizing President Clinton's goal of allowing victims and their families to receive appropriate compensation for airline accidents without facing the prospect of decades of litigation," Transportation Secretary Federico Pena said in a written statement.
The United States had been under pressure from the International Air Transport Association (IATA), the body that links the world's 232 major carriers, to approve the agreements.

Pena said the department had deferred action on a number of objections to the accords to allow passengers to benefit immediately from the carriers' voluntary waiver of the limits "while it considers ways to enhance the agreement."
